summary30Seconds: Securities Premium utilization (Section 52(2)): 1. Issue fully paid bonus shares, 2. Write off preliminary expenses, 3. Write off share/debenture issue expenses/commission/discount, 4. Premium on redemption of preference shares/debentures, 5. Buy-back of shares.
Pro-rata Allotment: Excess application money is adjusted towards allotment; on forfeiture, Share Capital A/c is debited with CALLED-UP value, Share Forfeiture credited with amount ACTUALLY RECEIVED.
Capital Reserve on Re-issue: Profit on reissue of forfeited shares = (Credit in Forfeiture per share - Discount on reissue per share) $\times$ Number of shares REISSUED.

coreConcepts.title: Share Capital: Classes, Pro-Rata Allotment & Calls
coreConcepts.content:
**Share Capital Categories**:
1. **Authorized (Nominal) Capital**: Maximum share capital stated in Memorandum of Association.
2. **Issued Capital**: Part of authorized capital offered to the public for subscription.
3. **Subscribed Capital**:
   - *Subscribed and fully paid-up*: All calls made and paid in full.
   - *Subscribed but not fully paid-up*: Calls made but in arrears, or company has not called up full face value.

**Calls-in-Arrears and Calls-in-Advance (Table F of Companies Act 2013)**:
- **Calls-in-Arrears**: Money called but not received. Interest charged up to **10% p.a.**
- **Calls-in-Advance**: Money received prior to call. Interest paid up to **12% p.a.** (paid even if there is no profit).

**Pro-Rata Allotment**:
When shares are over-subscribed, allotment is made proportionately.
$$\text{Allotment Ratio} = \frac{\text{Shares Allotted}}{\text{Shares Applied}}$$
$$\text{Excess Application Money} = (\text{Applied} - \text{Allotted}) \times \text{Application Money per share}$$
Excess is adjusted towards allotment and calls as per agreement.
ncertPointers: Minimum Subscription (Section 39): 90% of the issued amount must be subscribed within 30 days of prospectus issue; otherwise application money must be refunded within 15 days.
Securities Premium Account cannot be used for paying dividends or general reserves.

coreConcepts.title: Forfeiture & Re-issue of Shares & Capital Reserve
coreConcepts.content:
**Journal Entry for Forfeiture of Shares**:
$$\text{Share Capital A/c Dr. [No. of shares } \times \text{\textbf{Called-up value per share}}]$$
$$\text{Securities Premium A/c Dr. [If premium was NOT received]}$$
$$\quad \text{To Calls-in-Arrears A/c [Unpaid calls amount]}$$
$$\quad \text{To Share Forfeiture A/c [Amount \textbf{already received} excluding premium]}$$

*Rule for Securities Premium*:
- If premium was **already received**: DO NOT reverse/debit Securities Premium.
- If premium was **not received**: DEBIT Securities Premium A/c.

**Re-issue of Forfeited Shares**:
- Shares can be reissued at par, premium, or discount.
- **Maximum Permissible Discount on Re-issue**: Cannot exceed the amount forfeited (credited to Share Forfeiture A/c) on those reissued shares.
- Re-issue at discount:
  $$\text{Bank A/c Dr. [Amount received]}$$
  $$\text{Share Forfeiture A/c Dr. [Discount on reissue]}$$
  $$\quad \text{To Share Capital A/c [Paid-up value]}$$

**Transfer to Capital Reserve**:
$$\text{Capital Reserve} = \left( \frac{\text{Total Forfeited Amount}}{\text{Total Forfeited Shares}} \times \text{Shares Reissued} \right) - \text{Discount on Re-issue}$$
$$\text{Share Forfeiture A/c Dr. to Capital Reserve A/c}$$
ncertPointers: Balance left in Share Forfeiture Account (for shares not yet reissued) is shown under Share Capital as an addition to Subscribed Capital in the Balance Sheet.

coreConcepts.title: Debentures: Issue Conditions & Collateral Security
coreConcepts.content:
**Issue of Debentures with Redemption Conditions (6 Cases)**:
1. Issued at Par, Redeemable at Par: Standard par entry.
2. Issued at Discount, Redeemable at Par: Discount on Issue of Debentures Dr.
3. Issued at Premium, Redeemable at Par: Securities Premium Cr.
4. Issued at Par, Redeemable at Premium:
   $$\text{Loss on Issue of Debentures A/c Dr. to Premium on Redemption of Debentures A/c}$$
5. Issued at Discount, Redeemable at Premium:
   $$\text{Loss on Issue A/c Dr. [Discount + Redemption Premium]}$$
   $$\quad \text{To Debentures A/c [Face value]}$$
   $$\quad \text{To Premium on Redemption A/c [Redemption Premium]}$$
6. Issued at Premium, Redeemable at Premium:
   $$\text{Loss on Issue A/c Dr. [Redemption Premium] to Premium on Redemption A/c [Redemption Premium]}$$

**Debentures as Collateral Security**:
- Secondary security given to bank against a loan in addition to principal security.
- Two methods:
  - *Method 1*: No journal entry; only a footnote in Balance Sheet under Long-Term Borrowings.
  - *Method 2*: $\text{Debenture Suspense A/c Dr. to Debentures A/c}$ (Debenture Suspense is deducted from Debentures in Balance Sheet).
ncertPointers: Premium on Redemption of Debentures is a personal liability account shown under Non-Current / Other Current Liabilities.
Loss on Issue of Debentures must be written off in the year of issue using Securities Premium first, then P&L statement.

keyFormulasAndTables.name: Capital Reserve Formula
keyFormulasAndTables.formula: \text{Capital Reserve} = (\text{Forfeited Amount per share} - \text{Discount on Reissue per share}) \times \text{No. of Shares Reissued}

keyFormulasAndTables.name: Section 52(2) Permissible Uses of Securities Premium
keyFormulasAndTables.formula: \text{1. Fully paid bonus shares; 2. Prelim expenses; 3. Issue expenses/commission; 4. Redemption premium; 5. Buy-back}

workedExamples.question: A company forfeited 1,000 shares of ₹10 each, fully called up, on which the shareholder had paid ₹3 on application and ₹2 on allotment, but failed to pay the first & final call of ₹5. Out of these, 600 shares were reissued as fully paid-up for ₹8 per share. What is the amount transferred to Capital Reserve?
solutionSteps: Step 1: Amount forfeited per share = ₹3 (application) + ₹2 (allotment) = ₹5 per share.
Step 2: Reissue price = ₹8 per share (fully paid ₹10 share) $\implies$ Discount on reissue = ₹10 - ₹8 = ₹2 per share.
Step 3: Profit on reissue per share = Forfeited amount per share - Discount on reissue = ₹5 - ₹2 = ₹3 per share.
Step 4: Number of shares reissued = 600 shares.
Step 5: Amount transferred to Capital Reserve = 600 × ₹3 = ₹1,800. Option A is exact.

workedExamples.question: XYZ Ltd. issued 10,000, 9% Debentures of ₹100 each at a discount of 5%, redeemable at a premium of 10% after 5 years. What is the total amount debited to 'Loss on Issue of Debentures Account'?
solutionSteps: Step 4: Total Loss on Issue of Debentures = Discount on Issue + Premium on Redemption = ₹50,000 + ₹1,00,000 = ₹1,50,000.

commonTraps.misconception: Debiting Share Capital with face value (e.g. ₹10) when only ₹7 was called.
commonTraps.correctUnderstanding: Share Capital is debited STRICTLY with the **CALLED-UP VALUE** per share up to the stage of forfeiture.

commonTraps.concept: Capital Reserve Calculation on Partial Reissue
commonTraps.misconception: Transferring the entire balance of Share Forfeiture to Capital Reserve.
commonTraps.correctUnderstanding: Only the proportionate profit on SHARES ACTUALLY REISSUED is transferred. The balance belonging to un-reissued shares stays in Share Forfeiture A/c.

practiceQuestions.question: As per Table F of Companies Act 2013, the maximum rate of interest chargeable on calls-in-arrears is:
practiceQuestions.explanation: As per Table F, the board of directors can charge interest on calls-in-arrears @ 10% p.a. from the due date to the date of actual payment.

practiceQuestions.question: Which of the following is NOT a permitted use of the Securities Premium Account under Section 52(2) of the Companies Act, 2013?

options.text: Issue of fully paid bonus shares
Payment of cash dividends to shareholders
Writing off preliminary expenses of the company
Providing for the premium payable on redemption of preference shares

practiceQuestions.explanation: Section 52(2) prohibits the use of securities premium for payment of dividends.

practiceQuestions.question: On forfeiture of shares, the Share Capital Account is debited with:
practiceQuestions.explanation: Share Capital Account is debited with the amount called-up on the forfeited shares up to the date of forfeiture.

practiceQuestions.question: The maximum permissible discount that a company can allow at the time of reissue of forfeited shares is:

options.text: The amount previously forfeited on those shares

practiceQuestions.explanation: The discount allowed on reissue of forfeited shares cannot exceed the amount already received and credited to the Share Forfeiture Account on those specific shares.

practiceQuestions.question: When debentures are issued as collateral security against a bank loan, under Method 2, which account is debited?
practiceQuestions.explanation: When recorded by entry, the journal entry is Debenture Suspense A/c Dr. to Debentures A/c.

practiceQuestions.question: A company forfeited 200 shares of ₹10 each on which ₹6 per share (including ₹1 premium) was received. The amount credited to the Share Forfeiture Account will be:
practiceQuestions.explanation: Securities premium once received cannot be transferred to or credited to Share Forfeiture Account. Amount credited = 200 × (₹6 - ₹1 premium) = 200 × ₹5 = ₹1,000.

practiceQuestions.question: Premium payable on redemption of debentures is a:
practiceQuestions.explanation: Premium on redemption of debentures is a liability payable to debenture holders in future; hence it is a Personal Account shown under Non-Current / Other Long-Term Liabilities.

practiceQuestions.question: According to SEBI guidelines, what is the minimum subscription required before a company can proceed with allotment of shares?
practiceQuestions.explanation: As per SEBI guidelines and Section 39 of Companies Act, minimum subscription is 90% of the entire issue.

practiceQuestions.question: Balance remaining in the Share Forfeiture Account after reissue of all forfeited shares is transferred to:
practiceQuestions.explanation: Profit on reissue of forfeited shares is a capital profit and is transferred to Capital Reserve Account.

practiceQuestions.question: When shares are issued to promoters for their incorporation services, which account is debited?
practiceQuestions.explanation: When shares are issued to promoters for services rendered, Incorporation Costs A/c or Goodwill A/c is debited and Share Capital is credited.
